headline: A 2014 law extends, through 2015, the one-year protection that keeps lenders from foreclosing on some property owned by service members before their military service.
what_it_does: Under the law, a court may pause enforcement actions on a debt tied to property a service member owned before military service. A sale, foreclosure, or seizure of that property is invalid without a court order or a waiver signed by the service member. The law extends this one-year period through calendar year 2015 and brings back the older nine-month period starting January 1, 2016.

who_it_affects.group: Service members who owned property before their military service
who_it_affects.how: They can get court-ordered pauses on enforcement of debts tied to that property and cannot lose it to a sale or foreclosure without a court order or a signed waiver during the protected period.

who_it_affects.group: Lenders and loan servicers holding debts on such property
who_it_affects.how: They must get a court order or a signed waiver before selling, foreclosing on, or seizing covered property during the protected period, and courts may pause their enforcement actions.

who_it_affects.group: Courts handling enforcement cases involving service members
who_it_affects.how: They have the authority to stay proceedings to enforce obligations on covered property during the protected period.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted December 18, 2014. The one-year protection period applies through calendar year 2015, and the nine-month period takes effect January 1, 2016.
